turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. Who decided to put a zero in the gradebook before anyone picked up a phone and called me?
Upset. Who decided, Hale, and when?
But I'm not changing the grade.

On what basis? If the answer is that checker, your own procedure says software alone doesn't establish anything, and I have it printed in my bag. Give me something else, or I'm in the principal's office at 4:41.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

"I'm still not changing it." I'm writing that down, next to the fact that Owen found out from his phone in the middle of a class and nobody called me first. Is there a single document with a date on it, Hale, or is that the whole case?
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.

Then you're refusing to show me a single thing before I go upstairs. Fine, Hale: I'll ask the principal to review it today, and if that goes nowhere, the board under section 42. Last chance to put something with a date on it on this desk.
